Property Management in Phuket: Rental Fees and Owner Responsibilities

What a manager does and what it costs
HomeGuidesProperty Management in Phuket: Rental Fees and Owner Responsibilities

Ownership and costs · Last reviewed: 2026-11-26

If you do not live in Phuket all year, a management company can look after your condo or villa: find guests or tenants, handle cleaning and repairs and send you the income. Fees vary by company, property and service scope, and the figures below are indicative, not fixed rates or Nightdestiny prices.

What a management company does

  • Marketing and listings on Airbnb, Booking.com and other platforms.
  • Reservations, guest communication, check-in and check-out.
  • Cleaning, laundry and maintenance coordination.
  • Monthly reporting and payment of the owner's share.
  • Inspections and a contact point while you are abroad.

Indicative fees and how they are charged

There is no official rate in Thailand. Published guides show ranges like these, and an individual company may charge more or less:

Rental typeIndicative management fee
Short-term holiday rentals15–30%
Medium-term rentals15–20%
Long-term rentals8–15%

Companies may charge a percentage of gross revenue, of revenue after booking-platform fees or of revenue after operating costs, or a fixed monthly fee, sometimes plus a one-time tenant placement fee. Short-term lets need more guest service and cleaning, so their rates are typically higher than long-term lets.

Example: a 30% commission and other costs

Illustration only, assuming the commission is calculated on gross monthly revenue:

ItemAmount
Monthly rental revenueTHB 100,000
Management commission (30%)THB 30,000
Remaining before expenses and taxes (70%)THB 70,000

The remaining THB 70,000 is not your profit. Management commission is separate from the property's own expenses and from taxes: electricity, water and internet; cleaning, laundry and supplies; repairs, air conditioning servicing and, for villas, pool and garden care; condominium common area fees and sinking fund; insurance; and applicable taxes, which depend on your situation. Some of these are paid from rental income and some are billed to you, depending on the agreement.

Before you sign

  • What is the percentage, and what is it calculated on?
  • Which services are included, and which cost extra?
  • How often are you paid and do you get a monthly report?
  • Is there a repair spending limit that needs your approval?
  • What are the owner-use conditions, contract length and termination terms?

Short-term rental: legal points

Short-term rentals in Thailand can fall under the Hotel Act, which requires a licence, and stays of less than 30 days are generally treated as hotel use. Condominium rules may also restrict short stays. Requirements are changing, so confirm them for your building with a qualified Thai lawyer and your manager.

Frequently asked questions

How much does property management cost in Phuket?

Rates vary by company, property and service scope. Published indicative ranges are about 15–30% for short-term lets and 8–15% for long-term lets. Ask for the percentage, calculation basis and included services in writing.

Is rental income guaranteed?

No. Income depends on the property, season, pricing, management and the rules that apply.
